ost.outcome: A user of rn sees what they asked for work on the real thing early in a run, and grows it from there.

opportunities.opportunity: I see what I asked for work on the real thing early.
opportunities.by: #86: 6,079 lines before the first real check in #85

opportunities.opportunity: I pick what to meet first, without spelling out every detail.
What I first touch already holds the quality its kind needs.
It works in a large existing app, aimed at what I'm after now.

solution.solution: Rebuild rn as prompts and work scripts on one steering file per run, its opportunity solution tree for the moment's goal, making the least solution as one walking skeleton.
solution.why: It puts something that runs in the user's hands before most is made, and keeps no tree of the whole product to maintain.

assumption.assumption: Given the opportunities on the ost, the pruner keeps every named one, the user can pick, and the run reaches a real check before most deliverables are made.
assumption.test: Run rn from this branch on #62 up to the first real check; count what was made by then.
assumption.result: Failed on #62 (2026-11-26): the hearing and the pick held, and every named need stayed, but after 1h20m the run had made 7 of 10 deliverables, 834 lines, with nothing the user could try, as each put-up pushed through the repository's checks, which pulled in tests, coverage, check.sh, and trace.py before the hook that runs it; and its messages spoke of rn's insides while roles worked. Failed again on #62 (2026-11-27): after 20 minutes, 0 of 8 deliverables were done, as the repository's checks on each put-up drew in a LICENSE twice, a passed deliverable was made again, the riskiest assumption waited for all 8, the search for what exists read one page and showed the user nothing, and messages fell back into English after a pruner.

opportunities.opportunity: From there, I grow it one addition at a time, and keep each thing I asked for.
A mend I ask for lands at once.
An addition keeps the quality of what's there.
No need I named is dropped without my say.
At the end, I decide what happens to what I didn't pick.

decisions.decision: Talk with the user in Japanese and write each deliverable in English, as the user reads Japanese and the repository is in English.
Pile up the vital few and cut the trivial many thoroughly, as rn's center.
Make the least solution as one walking skeleton and check its riskiest assumption on the real thing first, so the run knows it reaches the goal before it builds much.
Make the opportunity solution tree for one run, so rn aims at the moment's goal, in a large existing app too.
Put each opportunity that people name on the tree for the user to pick, as the user decides what's dropped, not a role.
Show the opportunities in the user's words, numbered, with rn's pick and its grounds, so the user judges only which one brings the outcome closest.
Have the user give feedback as one who uses it, and rn settle how it's made and explain the solution only when asked, so the user's time goes to what only they can judge.
Make the least, and use the best practices in full on what's made, so less made costs no quality.
Propose at the run's end what to do with each unpicked opportunity, so the user decides what stays.
Keep the steering in one file with one writer to each part, so no part has two writers.
Make a unit case for each class that an interface's contract treats apart, with C0 and C1 at 100%, so each requirement has its case and no line lacks a requirement.
Have the user run the walking skeleton as the E2E check, so what works is judged by one who uses it.

Add a test above the unit level only for a fault that the user's run found and that should have been caught before it, or for an operation that can't be undone, so tests grow from evidence, not from what the design draws.
Make a test design or a test implementation only when a key result needs what the user's run can't show, such as a measure over many runs, so no test machinery is built ahead of need.
Make a deliverable in Rounds only when it's first made or remade, against every condition of its best practice, so its first quality is built in before the user touches it.

Make a change that adds what the people can do in Rounds for the added part alone, with the evaluator judging only the conditions it touches, as only one who tries it as the people would sees whether it serves them.
Call an opportunity 「できるようにしたいこと」 to rn's users, as they don't know the opportunity solution tree.
Work one step at a time, in order, and remove the old before making the new, so the branch never holds two ways at once.
Keep tests green and push on each commit, so each step stands on checked work.
Do the work alone, with no subagents, so one judgment keeps documents, scripts, and prompts in step.
Give work outside #86's purpose its own issue, herdr worktree, and pull request, so it reaches main without waiting.
Speak to the user in plain words, never in rn's or the plan's own terms, so the user follows without learning them.
Leave issue #86 as it was asked, as it's the request that started the work.
Keep /rn:on, /rn:up, /rn:dn, /rn:ty, and /rn:gm, so the user starts, stops, picks up, approves, and asks for a mend each by its own command.
Check the pull request whole before the merge is proposed, as any careful team does.
Leave the pull request's CI to the user, who sees it on the pull request before they merge, as waiting for it brings nothing in the user's hands earlier.
Have /rn:up go on with the run of the branch the user is on, and ask which only elsewhere, so the user names the run by where they type.
Write each prompt's steps by their purpose and intent, checked against every condition of the prompt best practice, so the AI judges a case the steps don't name.

Write each message to the user in one shape, with no heading such as 「いま：」: first one sentence of what was done, with how far the run is to the try as (2/4) where it counts, then what the user does now, either one question with numbered options, each with a line on what it leads to and the recommended one marked, or the command to try, and nothing after it. List once, when making starts, what is made before the try. At a role's end with nothing for the user to do, write the first part alone, in the terms of their need, never of rn's insides, so the user always sees how far the run has come and gives feedback at once, as Spec Kit and AI-DLC report progress against the plan shown first.
Call a run off on the user's words, such as 中止して, once they confirm what goes, removing its worktree, branch, and pull request, as rn 0.11.0 did, and keep /rn:dn for a stop for now.

Have the orchestrator hear from the user whom the run is for and what for, one question at a time, and hand the hearing to a pruner only once it is whole, as rn 0.11.0 did, since a pruner can't talk with the user and a request needs no issue.
Show the pick as the question, then each need numbered in the user's words alone, with no restated outcome and no means, the recommended one marked with why in one sentence.

Write each role's prompt in domain/ in three sections, Role, what the role is expected to achieve, Steps, each step's purpose and intent with only the plugin's own rules, and Output, what it hands back, as the entries hold the form that Claude Code fixes, so each line changes what the AI does.
Rewrite every prompt at once, with no reading through with the user, as the user asked for all of them fixed.

Write each role's prompt from the architecture and the prompt best practice: its Role from its component's line, its steps from its arrows in the sequences with the intent of their rules and strategies, and only the plugin's rules beside them, then trace both ways, so that what rn has built up stays in the architecture and nothing in a prompt comes from nowhere.

Where the user works in herdr, open each run's worktree in a workspace of herdr, and have herdr remove it on a cancel, else keep Claude Code's default place, as the user finds the run's worktree where they work, and herdr shows only those it holds.

Grow the run in this pull request: after the walking skeleton, ask at the run's end of each need left whether to make it now or keep it in an issue, and make each one picked as the walking skeleton was, one addition at a time, as the second mode is only that.
Write the outcome in the steering as a user story, who, what they want, and what for, as it's the form the hearing already asks.
Leave the repository's checks to the roles' judgment, with no step for them, as following a repository's rules goes without saying.
Have a SubagentStop hook check each role's result before the role ends, so that the role mends it itself and the orchestrator starts no role again.
Ask the user one question at a time, and have the script give only one, so that each can be talked over.
Give the pruner no step of its own to look for what exists, as the measure's question of the least holds it.
Have a SubagentStop hook take the pruner's result into the steering, so that the steering keeps one writer, by the single-writer principle, and the orchestrator has no step for it.

Write vital-few.md from zero as its purpose, to pile up the vital few and cut the trivial many thoroughly, its intent, and one criterion: without it, would its people be at a loss, answered from the user's words or a use's result, resting on the steering alone.
Have the refactorer, a role of its own, make the Round of refactoring, apart from the generator.
Write the generator's steps apart for a deliverable made new, one made again on the evaluator's findings, and one added to what's there, as each asks a different thing.
Have the generator mend where its people would be at a loss, and ask the user only where the mend needs a decision of theirs changed.
Have the generator hand back only the files it wrote or a question, as the evaluator judges each condition with its lines, and no one is at a loss without the generator's copy of them.
Take out of the evaluator the step for a deliverable that adds to what's there, as trying it as its people use it toward their aim already takes the addition.
Keep what is particular to a kind, such as running tests for code, in that kind's best practice, and out of a role's prompt.

Make a deliverable by Rounds of the generator and the evaluator, have the fixer mend what the Rounds leave, and once the deliverable is whole, have the refactorer, a role of its own, refactor it by the kind's refactor best practice before the user tries it, as making and refactoring apart is the practice, and the user tries what it does for its people, which a refactoring keeps.

Tell the roles how to use a best practice, the purpose and the intent of each of its parts, in domain/references/generating-with-best-practices.md for the generator and the refactorer and domain/references/evaluating-with-best-practices.md for the evaluator, and move vital-few.md to domain/references/, as a role uses a best practice in full only once it knows why each part is there.
Have a role's prompt point to each reference by its path alone, never a word of its contents, as an AI that reads a summary works from it without opening the file.
Have the generator's and the refactorer's prompts differ only in their purpose, what they start from, and the best practice they use.
Have the pruner weigh each problem before the fixer gets it, and the fixer only mend, as a decision is weighed before the mend.

Have the fixer find, before it mends, how to confirm that nothing already there breaks, confirm it so, mend the least, and confirm it again the same way, naming no means such as a hook, as the means are the repository's.

Have the fixer remove no file a check leaves and report no check that fails elsewhere, as a file a check leaves is git-ignored or committed, and the confirming before the mend finds what fails elsewhere.
Push each commit of a run as it is made, and drop the link of the put-up to the push, as a commit kept only on the user's computer is lost with it.
Make a run's worktree by `herdr worktree create` where HERDR_ENV is set, else by git, as herdr shows only the worktrees it makes and rn needs no herdr.

Keep the fixer and the refactorer outside the Rounds, in this order: the Rounds make the deliverable, the user confirms what more they leave, the fixer mends it, the refactorer refactors the whole, and then the user tries it.

Have ccpm's pre-push hook run check.sh once in the working tree, as its duty is to keep a broken commit off the shared branch, CI's being to check the commits pushed in a clean environment; hold each best practice to its schema alone, and drop trace.py, as no one is at a loss without it.

Have the inspector review the pull request as its author would before asking for review, by the practice that its prompt holds, from GitHub's and Google's guides: that it agrees with every file already in the repository and the repository's rules, and its title and description with its diff and its issue; that it holds nothing its purpose doesn't need; and that it leaves nothing behind, such as a test, a document, or a commit not pushed. The practice stays in the prompt and out of rn's best practices, as the inspector checks the same for every pull request, and a best practice holds what differs by a deliverable's kind. What the people get is the evaluator's.

Have one command of the steering script mark a deliverable done in place of `repository put-up` and `steering deliverable done`, as a put-up no longer pushes; and rename `checked` to name the inspection passed, as the inspector holds that check.

Have a deliverable take at most LIMIT judged Rounds with no exception for a decision made since, and leave the more that remains to the user's confirming, so that no Round records how many decisions the run held when it started.

Have each commit that rn's scripts make push at once, and open the run's draft pull request on the first push where none is open, so that `repository put-up` goes, as the steering script's mark of a deliverable done commits it.
Commit a role's changes once it ends, so that the people's folder for a try is a clone of the run's branch alone, with no copy of uncommitted files over it.

Remove `repository diff`, as the inspector reads the pull request with git itself, and remove the remove script and rn's hook that sends deletes to it, as a role deletes nothing now: a try lies in the system's temporary folder, and a check's file is git-ignored or committed.

Add a SubagentStop hook that checks a role's result against its schema and keeps the role going until it holds, and that takes a pruner's result into the steering and commits it, in place of the orchestrator restarting a role or running `steering commit`.
Keep `repository new`, `runs`, `stop`, and `cancel`, and the shared modules form, practice, place, host, and fault, as each holds one responsibility that a run needs.
